findings.issue: Create()'s exception filter catches IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException/CryptoException/InvalidOperationException but omits Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.SqliteException, which SignIn() and Recover() both include. DbConnectionFactory.Open probes sqlite_master to validate the key, so opening a leftover admin.db with a freshly generated random key throws SqliteException. That state is reachable: Create deliberately writes the database before the key file ("The database is built first"), so a crash/kill in between leaves admin.db with no keys/admin.key, and the folder is user-writable by design (AdminHostPaths.GrantUsersWriteAccess), so a deleted key file produces the same. The exception escapes Create, and A01's CreateAccount() has only try/finally, so it escapes the render as an unhandled exception instead of showing AdminAr.Account.Create.CreateFailed — and every retry fails identically.
findings.fix: Add `or Microsoft.Data.Sqlite.SqliteException` to Create()'s `catch (Exception exception) when (...)` filter so it returns AdminAccountRefusal.StorageFailed. Additionally, in Create() before `_db.Open(databaseKey)`, when `File.Exists(_paths.DatabaseFile)` and no key file exists, move the stray file aside (e.g. rename to admin.db.orphaned-<timestamp>) or delete it — with no key file nothing in it can ever be opened again — so the retry the screen offers can actually succeed.

findings.issue:
The alerts panel head renders `

@AdminAr.Dashboard.AlertOfficeNoSetup

` whenever `_board.Alerts.Count > 0`. That string is «بانتظار إنشاء ملف الإعداد الأول», which is a statement about offices without a setup file — but the panel also raises AdminAlertKind.UndistributedChanges and AdminAlertKind.RevokedDevice. A board whose only alerts are undistributed changes or a revoked device therefore prints a sentence that is simply untrue (AGREEMENT item 15 requires user text that says what is actually the case). The A03 design puts a count there instead («مكتبان بانتظار ملف الإعداد»).
findings.fix: Compute the counts per kind from `_board.Alerts` (`Count(a => a.Kind == AdminAlertKind.OfficeWithoutSetup)` etc.) and render a composed line via a new `AdminAr.Dashboard.AlertsSummary(offices, changes, revoked)` built from the existing `Counting` helpers, wrapped in `<Bdi>`; or render the sub-line only when at least one OfficeWithoutSetup alert is present.

findings.issue: SerializeDetails rejects a details key if the key name *contains* any of "password, passphrase, secret, key, seed, recovery, code, wrap, token" case-insensitively, and it does so by throwing ArgumentException. The substrings "code" and "key" match the most ordinary field names admin-2 and admin-3 will want to log — office_code (A05's رمز المكتب للجرد), device_code, key_version (A07's office-key rotation) — so a perfectly secret-free audit row becomes an unhandled ArgumentException thrown out of a screen action. This undermines the shared extension point admin-1 is supposed to hand over, and the existing test only proves the false positives are rejected, never that a legitimate name is accepted.
findings.fix: Match whole name segments rather than substrings: split the key on '_' and camel-case boundaries and compare each segment with StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase against the forbidden list (so "office_code" and "key_version" pass while "recoveryCode" and "officeKey" still fail), or keep the guard but redact instead of throwing (write the row with the value replaced by "—"). Add a test asserting Audit.Write succeeds with details {"office_code":"PLN-01"} and {"key_version":"2"}.

findings.issue: ReadCodeFromImage refuses a file larger than MaxImageBytes with `Toasts.Show(AdminAr.Account.Recovery.ImageNoCode, ...)` — «لم يُعثر على رمز في هذه الصورة» — but the file was never decoded, so the message states something the tool did not establish and points the person at the wrong remedy ("try a clearer picture").
findings.fix: Add a string to AdminAr.Account.Recovery, e.g. `public const string ImageTooLarge = "هذه الصورة كبيرة جدًا. اختر صورة أصغر أو اكتب الرمز.";` and show it for the size refusal instead of ImageNoCode.

findings.issue: The footer hint is `@(IsCreated ? AdminAr.Account.Create.StartHint : AdminAr.Account.Create.StartHint)` — both branches are the same expression, so the ternary is dead and the text «بعد الإنشاء تُفتح لوحة الهيئة مباشرة» is shown in step one, where the button says «إنشاء الحساب والمتابعة» and no account exists yet. StartHint is also reused as the placeholder Desc of the empty sheet WStateCard, so one string carries three different jobs.
findings.fix: Add a hint of its own for step one (e.g. `CreateHint = "أكمل الحقول ثم أنشئ الحساب."`), use it for the not-yet-created branch, and remove the identical-branch ternary.

findings.issue: `AlertsAll` («عرض الكل») is declared but never rendered anywhere; the A03 design shows «عرض الكل ←» in the head of the تنبيهات panel. Either the design element is missing or the constant is dead.
findings.fix: Render it in A03Dashboard.razor's alerts panel head as a text button navigating through `AdminRoutes.ForTab(AdminAr.Tabs.AuditLog)` (which stays inert until admin-3 adds A11, exactly like the «تصدير ملف الإعداد» button already does), or delete the constant.

findings.issue: OnParametersSet calls ReadOrgSummary, which calls AdminDashboardService.Read() — roughly ten SQL statements including the three alert queries and the department aggregate — every time the layout's Body parameter changes (i.e. on every navigation), to use only the organisation name and three counts.
findings.fix: Add a narrow `AdminDashboardService.ReadOrgLine()` that selects org.name plus the three `COUNT(*) FROM org_units WHERE level = …` figures in one pass and call that from the shell, leaving Read() for A03.

findings.issue: GrantUsersWriteAccess grants BUILTIN\Users FileSystemRights.Modify with ContainerInherit|ObjectInherit over the whole tool root, which includes keys\admin.key. Any local standard account can therefore edit the plain-JSON key file to clear failedAttempts/lockedUntil (or copy back the admin.key.bak that AdminKeyFile.Save leaves beside it) and defeat the 5-attempt/30 s lock-out, or delete the file outright and destroy the only two wraps of the admin.db key — and with them the organisation's signing and agreement seeds, irrecoverably. The pattern is copied from Wakeel.Desktop, where many employees share one machine; the admin tool has exactly one user.
findings.fix: Grant Modify only on exports\, staging\ and logs\ and leave keys\ and admin.db with the ACL they inherit, so only the account that created the organisation (and administrators) may write them. If the counter must also be tamper-evident, MAC the counter fields under a key derived from the database key and refuse a key file whose MAC does not verify.

findings.issue: Two consecutive `<summary>` XML blocks precede `private const string UnknownActor`: the first one describes ForbiddenDetailKeys but is attached to UnknownActor, so the constant carries a duplicated/incorrect doc comment and the array below is undocumented.
findings.fix: Move the first `<summary>` block (the one about key names that may never appear in details) down so it sits directly above the `ForbiddenDetailKeys` field.

findings.issue: Create() wipes `databaseKey` in its finally block but never wipes `recoveryCode.KeyMaterial` (the 13-byte hundred-bit secret RecoveryCode holds), so it stays in the managed heap after the sheet has been handed over.
findings.fix: Add `CryptographicOperations.ZeroMemory(recoveryCode.KeyMaterial);` to the same finally block, after the wraps have been built. (The grouped display string unavoidably stays in the returned sheet until «ابدأ» drops it, which is the intended one-time display.)

missing_spec_items: A02: the design's «تذكر هذا الجهاز 8 ساعات» tick box is not built. Deliberate and disclosed — it would require a DPAPI machine wrap of the admin.db key, which would mean whoever carries the computer away opens the organisation's signing keys. Needs an owner decision, not a silent omission.

A01: the design draws a grid of twelve 8-character one-time codes («12 رمزًا تُستخدم كل منها مرة واحدة»); the build shows the B1 specification's single 20-character code plus its QR. The specification and Wakeel.Crypto's RecoveryCode both say one code, so the build is right and the image is stale — but the divergence needs an owner note.

A01: the design's sheet carries «رقم الورقة: 20260912/12046» and, after printing, a «طُبعت 12/09/2026 10:24» chip. Neither is implemented (the sheet shows organisation, issue date and administrator only).
A03: the design shows «عرض الكل ←» in the head of the تنبيهات panel. AdminAr.Dashboard.AlertsAll exists for it but nothing renders it.

A02: the design's standing note reads «يُقفل الدخول 15 دقيقة بعد 5 محاولات خاطئة»; the build follows the B1 specification's «30 ثانية تتضاعف». Specification wins, but the image and the text disagree and the owner should confirm which stands.
notes:
VERIFICATION RUN

Exactly the four commands were run and read in full: `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Admin.UI --no-dependencies` (0 warnings, 0 errors), `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Admin --no-dependencies` (0/0), `dotnet build tests/Wakeel.Admin.Tests --no-dependencies` (0/0), `dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Admin.Tests --no-build` → Passed! Failed: 0, Passed: 50, Skipped: 0. Warnings-as-errors clean throughout; no other project was touched and no file was modified by this review.

HOST ACTUALLY LAUNCHED AND DRIVEN (not just compiled)
src/Wakeel.Admin/bin/Debug/net10.0-windows10.0.19041.0/Wakeel.Admin.exe with --remote-debugging-port=9333 --window-size=1366x768 --data-folder=<temp>. http://127.0.0.1:9333/json/version answered (Edg/152.0.4191.66). I drove the whole first run over CDP and looked at the screenshots:
- A01 rendered styled and RTL (document.documentElement.dir = "rtl", three stylesheets loaded — the Razor SDK switch on Wakeel.Admin.csproj is genuinely required, the static-web-asset manifest is what serves _content/Wakeel.Design/* and Wakeel.Admin.styles.css). All four password rules present with Arabic-Indic numerals («١٢ حرفًا فأكثر», «حرف كبير وحرف صغير», «رقم واحد على الأقل», «رمز واحد على الأقل مثل ! أو #»).
- Filled the four fields, pressed «إنشاء الحساب والمتابعة»: the sheet appeared with the red «تُعرض هذه الورقة مرة واحدة فقط» panel, a 21-character grouped code (E1S9-J6XY-E9KC-HT3M-D8FM7) in an isolated monospace box and a real PNG QR beside it. «ابدأ» was disabled=true; after ticking «طبعتُ الورقة وحفظتها» it became enabled and navigated to "/".
- A03 rendered with the dark top bar (avatar, «سامي الحاج» / «مدير النظام», theme + sign-out icon buttons both carrying aria-label «المظهر الداكن» / «الخروج من الأداة»), exactly the seven DESIGN-GUIDE tabs in order, zero .w-sidebar elements, the page header «لوحة الهيئة» with «تحديث» + «تصدير ملف الإعداد», and the four KPI cards reading live zeroes. Compared against design/exports/preview/{light,dark}/A/A03 — layout, order and wording match.
- The log (<temp>/logs/wakeel-admin-20260916.log) holds one line, "Wakeel admin host starting up", and no errors. Process killed; no Wakeel.Admin and no msedgewebview2 child from that data folder survives.
- keys/admin.key on disk after the run contains only: the two wraps (kind=password, kind=recovery, each Argon2id 64 MB / 3 iterations / 2 lanes with its own salt), adminName, orgName, counters and timestamps. No secret material, no password, no code.

WHAT IS RIGHT
Storage and crypto are sound. The database key is random and lives only inside the two wraps, so a password change re-wraps rather than re-keys and the printed sheet keeps working (proved by Recover_KeepsTheSheetUsableAfterThePasswordChanges). The lock-out counter lives in admin.key precisely because the database cannot be opened while the password is wrong, and there is a test that it survives a restart. Org keys are generated once, sealed with the database key before the row is written, the root certificate is issued through DeviceCertificate.IssueOrgRoot(orgId, identity, now) and verified against the stored public key in a test, and OpenOrgIdentity hands out a disposable identity so the private material is never held between actions. admin.db is genuinely unreadable without the key (the test asserts "SQLite format 3" is not even in the file). Audit rows carry no secrets, and one test walks every row written across a whole create/fail/sign-in/recover sequence.

Composition is clean for the next two packages: AddWakeelAdmin(paths) + AddAdminAccount() with TryAdd throughout, three host seams (IAdminPrintService, IAdminImagePixels, IAdminWindow) each with a do-nothing default, AdminRoutes naming every A04–A11 route behind a `Built` set each sub-package adds to, and AdminAr split into Common/Account/Dashboard so admin-2 and admin-3 add their own partials without touching admin-1's. The one rough edge in that handover is finding 3 (the audit writer rejecting `office_code` and `key_version`).

The three csproj edits beyond "ProjectReferences only" are all justified and none introduces a package: QRCoder and ZXing.Net are already pinned centrally and used by Wakeel.UI; `<EmbeddedResource Include="Migrations\*.sql" />` is how the admin migration set travels; and the Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Razor switch on Wakeel.Admin is required for static web assets (I confirmed the three stylesheets load). The QRCoder PackageReference in Wakeel.Admin.csproj was pre-existing, not added here.

Tests assert real behaviour, not tautologies: the lock-out test advances a TestClock and checks 30 s then 60 s; the restart test constructs a second service over the same folder; the recovery tests round-trip the actual printed string, including the dashes-stripped lower-case form; the bUnit tests drive real inputs and read the disabled attribute off «ابدأ». One genuine blind spot the builder disclosed: no test decodes a real QR image, because that needs the WPF imaging stack.

RTL/bidi (item 55) holds up: dir="rtl" on the root, <Bdi> on every organisation name, administrator name, machine line and composed count, Bidi.Wrap on sentences composed in C#, `direction: ltr; unicode-bidi: isolate` on the recovery-code box, and I found zero physical direction properties (padding-left/right, margin-left/right, left:, right:, text-align: left/right) across every .razor.css in the package. Every icon-only button carries both a tooltip and an aria-label. A grep of every AdminAr string and every .razor for server/port/database/SQL/Argon/HTTP/JSON/PostgreSQL turns up nothing user-visible.

WHY "fix" RATHER THAN "accept"
Build and tests are green and the package is functionally complete, but three medium findings stand: the SqliteException gap in Create() that turns a recoverable storage state into an unhandled exception on the first screen of the product, the A03 alerts sub-line that states something untrue, and the audit writer that will throw on admin-2's and admin-3's ordinary detail names. All three are small, local edits inside admin-1's own files.
